title: How Interstellar’s Docking Uses Relative Motion to Turn Chaos into a Stable Target

brief.audience: Film lovers interested in visual storytelling
brief.viewer_problem: Struggling to see how camera framing clarifies chaotic motion
brief.promise: We’ll reveal the visual trick that makes the docking readable
brief.original_contribution: Visual analysis of relative motion in Interstellar’s docking sequence
brief.payoff: Matching the Endurance’s rotation to the station creates a clear frame of reference

reviews.evidence: Autonomous commissioning brief defines one viewer question and one visible scene-level payoff.
Groq vision inspected timestamped source frames; every beat is bound to one recorded observation and source range.
Narration was generated as one continuous take and force-aligned from the accepted recording.
Each shot uses a portrait crop centered from the inspected frame and three contained subject checkpoints.
Captions are derived from measured word times and constrained to the mobile-safe region and house CPS ceiling.
The final beat uses the chronologically last selected observation to resolve the opening visual question.
